note: Very thin. No chart existed and only one song could be tied to 1960 by a source: a film song dated by its film's release, with a retrospective (not year-specific) popularity statement. No foreign hit could be sourced to Malaya/Singapore for 1960.

Very thin. No home song could be sourced as a 1961 hit (P. Ramlee's 1961 films Ali Baba Bujang Lapok and Seniman Bujang Lapok have song lists but no source calling a song a hit). Foreign rows rest on memoir-level evidence around Cliff Richard and The Shadows' November 1961 Singapore/Kuala Lumpur shows, not on a chart.

Thin. Home rows are P. Ramlee film songs dated by film release (Ibu Mertua-ku, 7 Mar 1962; Labu dan Labi, 29 Aug 1962) plus retrospective statements that they are among his/Saloma's best-known songs; no year-specific popularity measure. The single foreign row is memoir-level.

Thin but partly year-specific: Mr Twister has 1963 sales figures and Malaysia Forever is documented as an instant radio hit around the September 1963 federation. The Tiga Bidara row rests on one fan blog. The only foreign row is a general statement (the Beatles song that gave pop yeh-yeh its name), not chart evidence.

Moderate. Shanty's 12 weeks at No. 1 on the Singapore chart, the Beatles single it displaced, and Cliff Richard's Radio Malaysia/Radio Singapore peaks are year-specific. Suzana is dated 1964 by most sources (one says 1963). The P. Ramlee/Saloma film songs (Madu Tiga, Feb 1964; Tiga Abdul, Apr 1964) and the Sangam song are dated releases with retrospective popularity statements only.

Moderate for English-language pop (press retrospectives name 1965 hits; foreign rows have Radio Malaysia/Radio Singapore peaks), weak for Malay-language songs: the two Malay rows are a fan blog's dated releases with general popularity statements. Pop yeh-yeh was taking off this year but no source dates a specific kugiran hit to 1965.

Moderate. Year-specific: A. Ramlie's records with The Rhythm Boys are described as big hits in Singapore and Malaysia in 1966 and Kenangan Mengusik Jiwa as charting on Radio Singapura from its 1966 debut; Do It Right has a seven-week No. 1 run (Singapore chart only); foreign rows have Radio Malaysia/Radio Singapore peaks. The remaining Malay rows are dated releases with general statements, mostly from one fan blog. Evidence for Singapore-based acts is counted as home because the Malay record and radio market stayed shared after August 1965.

Moderate. Year-specific home evidence comes from one collector blog (Menari Go-Go) that names 1967 hits, plus the A-Go-Go '67 film song; Si Baju Hijau is dated 1967 by Esplanade and 1968 by a fan blog. Foreign rows have Radio Malaysia/Radio Singapore chart peaks. Several well-known pop yeh-yeh hits (Tak Mengapa, Kenanganku, Hidup Bersama, Selamat Tinggal Pujaan) are omitted because no source dated them.

Mixed. Foreign rows are well supported by Radio Malaysia/Radio Singapore peaks. For home songs only Enam Belas Lilin has a year-specific claim (15 straight weeks on the Malaysian charts in 1968, per a collector blog); the Rafeah Buang rows are a fan blog's dated releases with general popularity statements. No year-specific source was found for P. Ramlee's 1968 Merdeka Studio film songs.

Thin for home songs: all three home rows are a fan blog's dated releases with general popularity statements, no year-specific chart or sales evidence. Foreign rows have Radio Malaysia/Radio Singapore peaks, except Get Back, which rests on an unattributed Wikipedia note.
